sentences.text: This extinct flamingo is distinguished from living relatives by a clear scar where the first toe attaches, whereas modern species have a reduced or missing hallux.
Its foot was broader and deeper than that of the largest sampled male greater flamingo.
The genus was described by Miller in 1963.
Remains were found in the Etadunna Formation mudstone on the western shore of Lake Palankarinna in Australia's Lake Eyre basin.
Robust finger bones and a well-developed first toe suggest it was more like a terrestrial wader, such as a stork or crane, rather than an aquatic flamingo.
Phoeniconotius belongs to the family Phoenicopteridae.
This extinct flamingo genus lived in Australia during the late Oligocene to the early Miocene.
